# Kyoto 5-Day Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A balanced Kyoto itinerary for **2025-10-12 to 2025-10-16** with a **USD 2,400** on-the-ground budget, keeping the pace moderate and avoiding hiking. I’ve built in **one museum day**, **one food-focused day**, and **one half-day for shopping/free time**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

| Day | Date | Theme | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Oct 12 | Arrival + Central Kyoto | Check in, easy walk around **Kyoto Station** and nearby streets | Visit **Nishiki Market** for a light lunch and first look at local foods | Relaxed dinner in **Gion** and an early night |
| 2 | Oct 13 | Classic Kyoto Sights | **Kiyomizu-dera** area at a gentle pace, using taxis/buses to limit walking | Explore **Higashiyama** lanes and cafés; keep the route short | **Gion** evening stroll, tea, or a quiet izakaya dinner |
| 3 | Oct 14 | Museum Day | Spend the morning at the **Kyoto National Museum** or **Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art** | Slow lunch nearby, then a second museum or gallery if desired | Free evening for rest, dessert, or a simple neighborhood dinner |
| 4 | Oct 15 | Food-Focused Day | Market breakfast and a guided food walk or casual tasting stops | Lunch with a specialty Kyoto set meal; visit a sake or tea shop | Kaiseki, ramen, or yakitori dinner centered on local cuisine |
| 5 | Oct 16 | Shopping + Departure Prep | **Half-day free for shopping** in **Shijo-Kawaramachi** or **Teramachi** | Pack, check out, and keep the afternoon open for transfers | Final casual meal before departure |

## Budget Allocation Plan

Suggested split for the **USD 2,400 total** budget:

- **Lodging: USD 1,000–1,250**
- **Food & drinks: USD 500–650**
- **Local transport: USD 120–180**
- **Admissions & activities: USD 180–260**
- **Shopping buffer: USD 150–250**
- **Contingency: USD 100–150**

Budget shape by category:

- Lodging: **42–52%**
- Food & drinks: **21–27%**
- Transport: **5–8%**
- Admissions & activities: **8–11%**
- Shopping buffer: **6–10%**
- Contingency: **4–6%**

### Budget Chart Suggestion
Use a **donut chart** or **stacked bar chart** with these segments:
- Lodging
- Food & drinks
- Transport
- Activities
- Shopping buffer
- Contingency

Recommended visual styling:
- Keep **Lodging** as the largest segment
- Use a distinct accent color for **Food-focused day spending**
- Highlight **Contingency** in a muted gray

## Packing Checklist by Category

### Travel Documents
- Passport
- Flight confirmation and hotel booking details
- Travel insurance info
- Copies of IDs and reservations
- Payment cards and some yen cash

### Clothing
- Comfortable walking shoes
- Light layers for October weather
- 5 days of outfits plus one spare top
- Light jacket or cardigan
- Socks and undergarments
- Compact umbrella or rain shell

### Toiletries
- Toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant
- Skincare and sunscreen
- Any prescription medications
- Hand sanitizer and tissues
- Small day bag or crossbody pouch

### Electronics
- Phone and charger
- Power bank
- Universal adapter if needed
- Camera if you plan to take photos
- Headphones

### Day-Use Items
- Reusable water bottle
- Small notebook or notes app for restaurant names
- Foldable tote for shopping
- Coin pouch for transit and small purchases

### Nice-to-Have Extras
- Portable laundry kit
- Snacks for transit
- Lightweight scarf
- Small first-aid items
- Zip pouches for receipts and tickets

## Quick Actions

- Kyoto tourism overview: https://kyoto.travel/en
- Kyoto National Museum: https://www.kyohaku.go.jp/eng/
- Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art: https://kyotocity-kyocera.museum/en/
